mainTopic: Learning the rules of מעילה from תרומה through the word חטא, and widening them with 'תִּמְעֹל מַעַל'
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא that defines מעילה as 'change', quoting a פסוק that uses מעילה for turning to idol worship. The ברייתא then asks about unclear cases: damage without benefit, benefit without damage, things attached to the ground, and an agent who carried out his mission. It answers with a גזירה שוה, because the word חטא appears both by תרומה and by מעילה. So every condition of the תרומה sin carries over. Damage and benefit must go together, by the same person, from the same item, at the same time, with a detached item, and a successful agent makes the sender liable. Next the ברייתא repeatedly asks whether limits from תרומה should also restrict מעילה. Each time the extra words 'תִּמְעֹל מַעַל' teach 'in any case'. This brings in benefit from items that cannot be damaged, eating and benefit by different people adding up, and separate eatings joining even years apart. The amud ends as the ברייתא begins one more such question, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse showing מעילה means turning away
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes quoting a פסוק that uses the word מעילה for turning away to idol worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...their fathers, and went astray after the בעלים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes a proof that started earlier. It quotes the end of a פסוק showing that מעילה means changing or turning away, like turning to idol worship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes people who 'did מעילה' against the God of their fathers by going after idols. So מעילה means taking something away from its proper purpose. Using הקדש for your own needs is the same kind of change.

keyTerms.meaning: Misusing הקדש; literally a 'change' or turning away from proper use
And they went astray
The בעל idols

phrases.english: their fathers, and went astray after the ba'al idols."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the proof that started earlier, showing that מעילה means a change from proper use.
steps.raayaObject: That the word מעילה means a change or deviation
steps.raayaSupportSource: A פסוק describing idol worship with the word מעילה

steps.title: Which cases count as מעילה?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether מעילה applies to damage without benefit, benefit without damage, things attached to the ground, or an agent who did his job.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think a person is liable if he damaged הקדש but got no benefit, or got benefit but caused no damage. One might also think he is liable for something attached to the ground, or that an agent who carried out his mission is the one liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא lists cases where the rules of מעילה are unclear. It is setting up the next step, where a פסוק will answer them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Comparing מעילה to idol worship might suggest that damage alone is enough, even with no benefit. Comparing it to a סוטה might suggest that benefit alone is enough, even with no damage. The ברייתא also asks about things still attached to the ground, and about who is liable when an agent does what he was sent to do.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One might think': it opens a possible mistaken idea
He damaged or lessened the item
He got benefit or use from it
Attached to the ground
An agent sent by someone else

steps.confusionAlert: The word יכול does not state the הלכה. It brings up a possible idea that the ברייתא is about to settle with a פסוק.

phrases.english: One might think: if he damaged but did not benefit,
phrases.notes: This fits the comparison to idol worship, where a person makes a change but gets no benefit.

phrases.english: or if he benefited but did not damage,
and with something attached to the ground,
and with an agent who carried out his mission?
phrases.notes: He means: is the agent himself liable, or the one who sent him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that מעילה has been compared to idol worship and other cases, the ברייתא asks how far those comparisons go.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether damage alone, benefit alone, attached items, or an agent's actions bring liability for מעילה, and who is liable

steps.title: The word חטא links מעילה to תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from the word 'וחטאה' and links מעילה to תרומה through the shared word חטא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'and sins'. 'Sin' is said about תרומה, and 'sin' is said about מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its questions with the word 'וחטאה' in the פסוק about מעילה. The same word 'חטא' appears by תרומה, so the two are compared.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a גזירה שוה: the same word in two places tells us to apply the rules of one to the other. The rules of תרומה will settle the doubtful cases from the previous step. The ברייתא spells out the details next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The פסוק teaches': it brings the answer from a פסוק
Sin: the shared word that links the two topics
The portion of produce given to a כהן
Comparing two laws because they share the same word

steps.whatToRemember: The rules of מעילה in unclear cases come from תרומה, because both share the word חטא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This comparison is the basis for the main rules about when a person is liable for מעילה.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "and sins."
"Sin" is said regarding תרומה,
and "sin" is said regarding מעילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the questions of the previous step by bringing a פסוק that links מעילה to תרומה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The unclear cases are settled by comparing מעילה to תרומה, through the word חטא that appears in both.

steps.title: The six conditions of תרומה carry over to מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא spells out the comparison. Every condition that applies to the חטא of eating תרומה also applies to the חטא of מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: With תרומה, a person is guilty when he damages and benefits, the same person damages and benefits, he benefits from the same thing he damages, the damage and benefit happen together, the item is detached from the ground, and an agent did his job. So too with מעילה: all the same conditions apply.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא completes the answer it started in the previous step. It lists exactly what we learn about מעילה from the word חטא that also appears with תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shared word חטא works like a bridge, so all six features of the תרומה sin cross over to מעילה and answer the earlier questions. For an item that can be damaged, damage alone or benefit alone is not enough; attached items are excluded, and an agent who did his job makes the sender liable. Steps 5 and 7 add that using an item that cannot be damaged still counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Damages or lessens the item, for example by using it up
Gets benefit or enjoyment
At the same time, together
Detached from the ground, not growing or built into the earth
An agent who carried out what he was sent to do
Learning a law from one topic to another because the same word appears in both

steps.whatToRemember: Through the shared word חטא, the basic מעילה needs damage plus benefit, by the same person, from the same item, at the same time, with a detached item. It also counts when it is done through a successful agent.
steps.whyThisMatters: These six conditions shape the basic definition of מעילה for the rest of the discussion. The very next step already begins to stretch beyond them.

phrases.english: Just as the word "sin" said about תרומה
phrases.notes: This is the sin of a non-כהן eating תרומה, which uses the same word חטא.

phrases.english: applies when one damages and benefits,
and the one who damaged is the one who benefits,
and he benefits from the same thing he damages,
and his damage and his benefit happen at once,
and with something detached from the ground,
and with an agent who did his job —
so too the word "sin" said about מעילה
applies when one damages and benefits,
and the one who damaged is the one who benefits,
and he benefits from the same thing he damages,
and his damage and his benefit happen at once,
and with something detached from the ground,
and with an agent who did his job.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the גזירה שוה between תרומה and מעילה that was introduced in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: All six conditions of the חטא of תרומה apply to מעילה. These are damage plus benefit, the same person, the same item, at the same time, a detached item, and a successful agent.

steps.title: Where do we learn that benefit without damage counts?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא points out that the comparison to תרומה only covers eating. It asks for a source that benefiting from an item that does not get damaged is also מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: So far I only know about someone who eats. From where do I know that someone who benefits from an item that does not get damaged is also guilty?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finds a gap in what it just learned and asks for a new source. This sets up the next part of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תרומה is about eating, so the comparison only proves מעילה for eating, where the item is used up. But many sacred items, like clothing or tools, can be used without being damaged. The ברייתא wants a source that this kind of use is also מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: I only know (so far)... — the source covers only this case
Damage or loss of value
From where (do we learn this)?

steps.confusionAlert: This does not contradict the earlier rule of 'damage and benefit.' The ברייתא is simply asking for a separate source to extend מעילה to use that does not cause damage.

phrases.english: I only have the case of one who eats;
and one who benefits from an item that does not get damaged,
from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Notes that the derivation in step 4 is limited to eating and asks for a source to extend it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that benefiting from a sacred item without damaging it is also מעילה.

steps.title: Where do we learn that eating and benefit combine?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks for a source that one's own eating or benefit and another person's eating or benefit add up together, even when they are spread over a long time.
steps.simpleTranslation: His eating and his friend's eating, his benefit and his friend's benefit, his benefit and his friend's eating, his eating and his friend's benefit all join together, even over a long time. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a second question for a source. This time it asks about adding up different acts of eating and benefit to reach liability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists four mixes of eating and benefit, by himself and by another person. It asks how we know they combine to reach the minimum amount for מעילה. The words 'even over a long time' show that the acts do not need to happen close together.

keyTerms.meaning: Combine, add up together
His fellow, another person
Over a long period of time
Eating and (other) benefit

phrases.english: his eating and his fellow's eating,
his benefit and his fellow's benefit,
his benefit and his fellow's eating,
his eating and his fellow's benefit
that they join together with each other,
phrases.notes: They join to reach the minimum amount, a פרוטה's worth, needed to be liable for מעילה.

phrases.english: even over a long time,
from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second question to the question in step 5, now about combining different acts to reach liability.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that eating and benefit, by oneself and another person, combine to reach the amount for מעילה, even over a long time.

steps.title: The extra words teach that מעילה applies in any case
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers the question from Step 6 with the words 'תִּמְעֹל מַעַל', which teach that מעילה applies in every case.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'תִּמְעֹל מַעַל', meaning: in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question it just asked in Step 6. The doubled words 'תִּמְעֹל מַעַל' show that מעילה applies in all cases, even when eating and benefit by different people add up together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison to תרומה alone would have limited מעילה to the kinds of cases found by תרומה. The Torah's extra wording, 'מעל' on top of 'תמעול', is read as including everything. That covers benefit without damage, and one person's use joining another's.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches; it introduces the source from the פסוק
'Commits a מעילה' (ויקרא 5:15); the doubled wording is read as including more cases
In any case; the rule applies in every situation

phrases.english: The verse states:
"Commits a misuse"
– in any case.
phrases.notes: The Torah could have said just 'תמעול', so the extra 'מעל' is read as stretching the rule to every case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question posed in Step 6 (and also covers Step 5).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The inclusive phrase 'תִּמְעֹל מַעַל' teaches that מעילה applies in any case, including when eating and benefit by different people combine.

steps.title: Do two separate eatings add up for מעילה?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that, like תרומה, מעילה should not combine two separate eatings. It then asks for a source that eating today and eating tomorrow do add up.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the comparison to תרומה holds, then just as by תרומה two eatings are not joined into one, so too by מעילה two eatings should not be joined. From where do we know that if someone ate today and ate again tomorrow, even after a long time, the two eatings join together?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a new problem with the comparison to תרומה. By תרומה, two separate eatings do not join into one, so maybe the same is true by מעילה. It asks for a source that they do join.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison through the word חטא could carry over a limit from תרומה: each eating stands alone there. The ברייתא wants to know how we know that by מעילה, small amounts eaten at different times add up to the minimum amount. This holds even with a long gap in between.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, then just as; it brings up a possible limit from the comparison
'Sin'; the shared word that links מעילה to תרומה
Combined; joined two smaller amounts into one
Two separate acts of eating
A long time

phrases.english: If so, just as the "sin" stated regarding תרומה
– does not combine two eatings as one,
so too the "sin" stated regarding מעילה
– should not combine two eatings as one.
From where do we know that if he ate today and ate tomorrow,
phrases.notes: He means he ate part of the amount today and the rest tomorrow, and the two parts should count together.

phrases.english: and even after a long time, [they combine]?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה ״חֵטְא״ הָאָמוּר בִּתְרוּמָה – לֹא צֵירַף שְׁתֵּי אֲכִילוֹת כְּאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new possible limit on the תרומה comparison after Step 7 closed the previous one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that separate eatings, even far apart in time, combine for מעילה.

steps.title: Separate eatings do add up, from the same extra words
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers again from 'תִּמְעֹל מַעַל': in any case, so separate eatings combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'תִּמְעֹל מַעַל', meaning: in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question about two eatings with the same inclusive words. By מעילה, eatings on different days do add up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The limit from תרומה, that each eating stands alone, does not carry over to מעילה. The inclusive phrase overrides it. Amounts eaten at different times join, even with a long gap.

keyTerms.meaning: An inclusion; extra wording in the פסוק that adds more cases
Joining small amounts together into the full required amount

phrases.english: The verse states:
"Commits a misuse"
– in any case.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The inclusive phrase teaches that separate eatings combine for מעילה, even over a long time.

steps.title: Does one person's eating join another person's eating?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא notes that by תרומה the damage and the benefit happen together. It then asks for a source that one person's eating combines with another's, even three years apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the comparison holds, then just as by תרומה the damage and the benefit happen together, [מעילה should be the same]. From where do we know that his eating and his friend's eating join together? And even from now until three years later, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises another possible limit from the comparison to תרומה. It asks how we know that two different people's eating can add up for מעילה, even years apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By תרומה, the damage to the food and the eater's benefit happen in one act by one person. That might suggest מעילה also needs one act by one person. The ברייתא asks for a source that two people's separate uses join, even with a gap of three years.

keyTerms.meaning: Its damage; the harm done to the item
His benefit; the use a person gets from the item
Together, at the same time
His friend's eating; another person's use

phrases.english: If so, just as the "sin" stated regarding תרומה
– its damage and his benefit are together,
from where do we know that his eating and his friend's eating [combine]?
And even from now until three years later,
from where do we know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה ״חֵטְא״ הָאָמוּר בִּתְרוּמָה – פְּגִימָתוֹ וַהֲנָאָתוֹ כְּאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a further limit on the comparison, now about two different people, after Step 9 settled separate eatings by one person.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that one person's eating combines with another person's eating for מעילה, even three years apart.

steps.title: Two people's eating also adds up
steps.stepSummary: Once more, 'תִּמְעֹל מַעַל' teaches 'in any case', so two people's eating combines even years apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'תִּמְעֹל מַעַל', meaning: in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the same answer: the inclusive words teach that one person's eating and another's join together for מעילה, even three years apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By מעילה, the damage and the benefit do not have to come together in one person's single act. Different people's uses, spread over a long time, add up to the required amount.

keyTerms.meaning: Three years; an example of a very long gap that still does not stop the joining

steps.whatToRemember: Each time the comparison to תרומה would limit מעילה, the extra words 'תִּמְעֹל מַעַל' (in any case) widen it. Separate eatings and different people's eatings all combine, even over long periods.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"Commits a misuse"
– in any case.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The inclusive phrase teaches that one person's and another person's eating combine for מעילה, even three years apart.

steps.title: Starting another comparison to תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא begins yet another 'just as by תרומה' line. The rest continues past this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as the 'sin' stated regarding תרומה...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The ברייתא is starting one more possible limit from the comparison to תרומה, and the question itself continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same pattern is repeating: suggest a limit from תרומה, then ask for a source. Here only the opening words appear. The actual limit being raised comes right after this.

keyTerms.meaning: That is stated; the word as it appears in the Torah
A teaching that links two topics through a shared word, like חטא here

phrases.english: If so, just as the "sin" stated regarding תרומה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new round of the same pattern after Step 11 closed the previous one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The opening of another possible limit carried over from תרומה; the full question continues after this point.
